verdict.rationale: Slate is a conversational coding agent driven by natural-language prompts. Its docs show it can deeply research a user's problem, analyze a codebase, run shell commands and perform integration tests manually, which supports troubleshooting through natural-language queries. However, no first-party doc explicitly describes a debugging workflow; the troubleshooting page covers bug reports about Slate itself, which is off-topic. Missing for 10: explicit documented debugging/error-diagnosis workflow (e.g., stack-trace analysis, root-cause fixing), worked debugging examples, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can debug issues and troubleshoot using natural-language queries

citations.quote: Have slate in parallel deeply research your problem
Slate is one of the few agents capable of performing integration tests manually.
While one or more agents run in the background, you can keep talking with Slate
